drills.q: $5M position, 1.5% daily vol. 99% and 95% parametric VaR?
Scale a 1-day 99% VaR of $200K to 10 days. When is this wrong?
drills.a: $200K x sqrt(10) = ~$632K. Wrong under fat tails/vol clustering: multi-day tails grow faster than sqrt(t) when vol is autocorrelated; use overlapping bootstrap or explicit multi-day simulation for regulatory-grade numbers.

drills.q: 250-day year at 97.5% VaR: how many exceptions expected, and what's the Kupiec verdict if you see 12?
drills.a: Expected 6.25. LR_POF with x=12, T=250, p=0.025 gives LR well above 3.841 -> reject the model at 5%. At 97.5% there is enough signal to catch doubling of the true rate within a couple of years - unlike 99%.

drills.q: Why does ES97.5 punish a short-put book more than VaR99 does?
drills.a: Short puts have extreme negative skew: losses concentrate just past the quantile. VaR99 measures only where the tail starts; ES averages the whole loss region beyond it, so skewness and kurtosis translate directly into higher capital.

drills.q: Your desk's exceptions: 3 in the last year, but all within one fortnight. Pass or fail?
drills.a: Count passes (green zone) but conditionally suspicious: clustering violates iid; Christoffersen independence test likely rejects. Root cause: unconditional window entering a vol shock -> move to GARCH-filtered VaR and report conditional backtests alongside counts.

drills.q: Give the two-digitals subadditivity counterexample numbers.
drills.a: Two independent digitals each lose $100M w.p. 0.7%. Each 99%-VaR = $0 (prob below 1%). Combined P(any loss) = 1-(0.993)^2 = ~1.39% > 1%, so joint 99%-VaR ~ $100M > 0 + 0. Merging books increased measured risk - incoherent.

drills.q: Design a reverse stress test for a regional bank in three steps.
drills.a: 1) Define breach: CET1 < regulatory minimum under stress. 2) Choose shock dimensions (rate rise bp, deposit runoff %, spread widening bp). 3) Solve numerically for minimal combination breaching capital (e.g., +250bp AND 35% uninsured-deposit runoff). Report distance-to-breach as vulnerability magnitude.

drills.q: March 16 2020 vs Aug 5 2024 VIX spikes: what distinguishes them for risk design?
drills.a: Mar 2020: VIX peaked 82.69 amid a sustained regime break - SPX fell ~34% over 23 sessions, correlations broke, liquidity vanished for weeks. Aug 2024: intraday spike above ~60 that mean-reverted in days (carry unwind). First breaks capital math; second breaks intraday/stop-loss logic and leverage cascades. Different instruments need different overlays.
